Specimen.sentence: We design identities that stay legible over time.
Specimen.paragraph: Every project starts from a single question: what has to remain once everything else has gone out of fashion. We work by subtraction, because empty space is not what is left around the content — it is part of the content.

Styleguide.title: Styleguide
Styleguide.intro: Control surface for the design system. Every value shown here is read from the same tokens the CSS is generated from: if a check passes on this page, it passes on the site.

colors.title: Colour
colors.description: Level 1, primitives: the only file to touch when the identity changes. Level 2, semantic roles: what components actually see.
colors.currentTheme: Values of the theme currently active.

contrast.title: Contrast check
contrast.description: WCAG 2.1 ratios computed on both themes, not assumed. Text: AA requires 4.5. Borders and non-text elements: 3.
contrast.allPass: Every required pair passes AA on both themes.
contrast.someFail: Some pairs do not reach the AA threshold.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Seven grades, fluid scale in clamp(). Three weights only: 300, 400, 500. Hierarchy is built with scale and space, never with weight.
typography.cjkNote: Chinese carries a 6% optical compensation and 2.0 leading: the difference is visible across the three lines of each grade.

spacing.title: Space
spacing.description: 4px base with geometric jumps, extended upwards because empty space is content. Off-scale values do not exist as utilities.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Four durations, a single easing for every reveal, stagger between 80 and 120ms. Movement is slow, decelerated and quiet: translation plus opacity, never scale or rotation.
motion.reducedMotionNote: With prefers-reduced-motion on, transitions are flattened site-wide by a single rule.

shape.title: Shape and grid
shape.description: Zero radius on content blocks and media. Wide continuous corners only on glass elements: content is paper, the interface is a screen.
shape.gridNote: 12 columns on desktop, 6 on tablet, 4 on mobile. Resize the window to see it change.

glass.title: Glass
glass.description: One component, GlassSurface, holds all four layers: backdrop blur, adaptive fill, specular edge and refraction. No other component implements glass on its own. It applies to the floating interface layer only: content stays opaque and flat.
glass.sample: Content is paper, the interface is shoji.

proof.title: Contrast proof on glass
proof.description: Text on glass does not sit on a colour, it sits on the fill composited over whatever scrolls beneath. The worst case is not a photograph: it is pure white under the dark theme and pure black under the light one. Hold the ratio on those two and it holds on any image.
proof.allPass: Text on glass keeps AA on both extremes, in both themes.
proof.someFail: Text on glass loses AA on at least one extreme.

glass.floors: Minimum opacity computed from the palette: {light} on the light theme, {dark} on the dark one. The floor stated by the specification is {spec}; the token generator refuses to emit a fill more transparent than the higher of the two.
glass.budget: At most {limit} glass surfaces at once. The count is enforced at runtime: going over logs an error rather than quietly costing frames.
glass.fallback: Without backdrop-filter the panel turns opaque, never invisible. The same applies to readers who ask the system for less transparency.
glass.noBlurAnimation: The blur radius is never animated: only opacity and transform are declared transitionable on glass.

aliases.title: Roles and utilities
aliases.description: Level 3. Components never write a colour: they use these utilities, which point at the semantic roles.
